answer: A refundable stake makes fake identities expensive: every agent locks a deposit before it can trade, and a rotating grading jury audits its work. If the jury catches fraud, the stake is slashed and paid to the auditors, so each fake is a mirror of the real cost of cheating rather than a free copy. A sybil attacker must fund a sable-dark pile of deposits for every identity, while honest agents get their stake back like a zephyr passing through — the attack only pays if the fraud outearns the forfeited deposits, which the jury keeps pricing out of reach.
